Summary: Epic 0: Engineering Foundation
Description: The development team has a reproducible deployment platform for local, testing, and AWS staging that includes environment configuration, PostgreSQL/Alembic, S3/ECR/IAM/networking, Jenkins/Terraform, observability, application shells, API mocks, and test harnesses before feature development.

Summary: 0.1 Standardize repository, environment and secrets configuration
Description:
As a developer,
I want a documented and reproducible configuration for local, test and staging environments,
So that I can run and verify HeritageGraph without relying on undocumented machine-specific settings or committing secrets.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a new clone of the repository
**When** developers follow the setup instructions
**Then** the backend and frontend can install dependencies using the specified runtime/package manager versions
**And** basic run, test and health checks are documented.

**Given** backend, frontend, data pipeline and observability components need configuration
**When** developers view sample environment files
**Then** every required variable is listed with a safe development description and value
**And** the sample file does not contain real credentials or secrets
**And** secret/runtime artifacts are removed from source control.

**Given** the application starts in local, test or staging
**When** required configuration is missing or malformed
**Then** the application stops prematurely with a message indicating an invalid configuration name
**And** does not write the secret value to the log.

**Given** the repository already has previous code and configuration
**When** this story is deployed
**Then** existing structures are reused or standardized instead of creating a new configuration system in parallel
**And** the changes do not remove the ability to run existing tests.

Summary: 0.2 Set up PostgreSQL, extensions and Alembic baseline
Description:
As a backend developer,
I want a reproducible PostgreSQL 16 database baseline for local, test and AWS staging,
So that schema changes can be developed, verified and deployed consistently.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** developer has completed environment configuration in Story 0.1
**When** start the local database according to the instructions
**Then** PostgreSQL 16 is ready via health check
**And** data is stored in managed volume
**And** database does not use credential production.

**Given** an empty database
**When** run Alembic upgrade to the latest revision
**Then** the existing schema baseline was successfully created
**And** the necessary `pgvector` and `pg_trgm` extensions are enabled
**And** rerun the migration without causing errors or creating duplicate objects.

**Given** migration changes the database
**When** CI or developer tests migration
**Then** upgrade is run on a clean database
**And** downgrade/rollback is checked when migration supports rollback
**And** migration errors cause checks to fail instead of being ignored.

**Given** backend connection to local, test or RDS staging
**When** the application starts
**Then** connection URL, pool and SSL behavior are obtained from environment configuration
**And** health endpoint differentiates API live state from database ready state
**And** credential/connection string does not appear in logs.

**Given** repository already has `schema.sql` and Alembic migrations
**When** sets baseline
**Then** the existing migration history is inventoried and used as the deployment source
**And** does not create a parallel schema or pre-create a table that only serves future stories.

Summary: 0.3 Provision AWS staging, storage and container foundation
Description:
As a platform developer,
I want a minimal, reproducible AWS staging environment,
So that HeritageGraph components can be deployed and integrated before feature development begins.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** AWS compute options are still open
**When** story begins
**Then** an ADR comparing the existing alternative, ECS/Fargate and EC2-based containers by cost, complexity, deployment time, inference and rollback
**And** ADR chooses the smallest option that meets staging/demo
**And** EKS or MWAA should not be selected without demonstrated need.

**Given** Valid AWS account and staging configuration
**When** apply infrastructure definition
**Then** staging has ECR container registry, S3 canonical bucket, necessary networking and IAM roles separated by responsibility
**And** infrastructure can be created or updated repeatedly without generating uncontrolled resources
**And** state and secrets are not committed to the repository.

**Given** RDS PostgreSQL staging is connected to the backend
**When** checks network access
**Then** RDS is not directly public
**And** only authorized workloads/roles can connect
**And** migration baseline from Story 0.2 runs successfully on staging.

**Given** backend image posted to ECR
**When** deploy to the selected compute target
**Then** public ingress only exposes the necessary endpoint over HTTPS
**And** the backend accesses RDS and S3 with appropriate IAM/configuration
**And** the frontend or smoke client can call the FastAPI health endpoint.

**Given** a raw document, manifest or test asset
**When** the workload is granted S3 write/read permissions
**Then** the object is saved under the specified prefix/policy
**And** the workload cannot perform actions beyond its minimum permissions
**And** S3 is still the canonical MVP object store, without critical-path dual-write to R2/Azure.

**Given** staging deployment error or needs to be removed
**When** operator follows the runbook
**Then** have a documented rollback/cleanup process
**And** resource ownership and expected costs can be checked.

Summary: 0.4 Automate Jenkins CI/CD and Terraform delivery
Description:
As a developer,
I want an automated delivery pipeline with enforceable quality gates,
So that changes reach AWS staging consistently and unsafe builds are rejected before deployment.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a pull request to change the backend, frontend, migration or infrastructure
**When** Jenkins pipeline runs
**Then** pipeline only runs relevant component checks but always applies lint/type checks and required tests
**And** failure at any required gate blocking build/deploy
**And** the results of each gate are clearly displayed.

**Given** changes include database migration
**When** pipeline checks migration
**Then** migration is run on a clean test database
**And** upgrade or rollback check errors cause the pipeline to fail
**And** staging cannot be migrated if the build has not passed previous gates.

**Given** changes to Terraform
**When** CI runs infrastructure checks
**Then** formatting, validation and planning are performed
**And** plans can be reviewed before applying
**And** The Jenkins deploy role is separate from the runtime roles and has only the necessary permissions.

**Given** branch/revision is allowed to deploy and has passed all gates
**When** pipeline builds and releases components
**Then** the container image is assigned an immutable revision tag and pushed to the ECR
**And** staging deploy to the correct image revision
**And** health/smoke checks run after deploy.

**Given** smoke check after failed deployment
**When** pipeline handles deployment failure
**Then** release is marked as failed
**And** the system rolls back to the last good revision or provides a documented rollback operation
**And** pipeline does not report false successes.

**Given** new model or prompt requires rollout
**When** delivery is configured
**Then** model/prompt rollout is a separate pipeline from software deployment
**And** does not automatically promote 10% → 50% → 100% if quality, grounding, latency or error gate have not been reached.

**Given** credential is used by Jenkins
**When** the pipeline logs or exports artifacts
**Then** secrets are obtained from the appropriate credential store
**And** token, password and connection string do not appear in log/artifact.

Summary: 0.5 Set observability baseline
Description:
As an operator,
I want correlated metrics, logs and traces across HeritageGraph,
So that I can detect failures and diagnose requests without exposing sensitive data.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a request goes through the frontend and FastAPI
**When** the request was processed successfully or failed
**Then** the system assigns or transmits correlation/trace ID
**And** structured logs have service, environment, severity, timestamp and correlation ID
**And** response/log does not reveal passwords, tokens, raw IP or sensitive personal data.

**Given** API and dependencies work
**When** Prometheus collects metrics
**Then** has a minimum request count, error count, duration histogram and dependency health
**And** metric labels do not contain unbounded values such as raw URLs, user input, or arbitrary entity IDs
**And** p50/p95/p99 can be calculated from the data obtained.

**Given** a request to call a database or internal service
**When** OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled
**Then** trace shows the path through the API and the appropriate dependency adapter
**And** error span retains enough metadata for diagnosis without containing secret or raw sensitive content
**And** the trace is sent to the configured Tempo/X-Ray target.

**Given** the application or pipeline writes structured logs
**When** Loki collects logs
**Then** operator can filter by service, environment, severity and correlation ID
**And** retention/configuration consistent with a documented demo environment.

**Given** a call to Qwen or grounded QA in the following stories
**When** Langfuse integration is used
**Then** trace contract supports model, prompt, corpus version, evidence IDs, token usage, latency and grounding result
**And** raw prompt/evidence is only saved according to the configured privacy policy
**And** observability failure does not cause the business request to fail.

**Given** telemetry baseline is running
**When** operator opens Grafana
**Then** dashboard displays service health, request/error rate and latency
**And** there is a baseline alert for service unavailable, error-rate spike and latency threshold
**And** dashboard/alert definitions are versioned.

**Given** a smoke request on AWS staging
**When** request completed
**Then** operator traces requests from health/API signal through logs and service trace
**And** smoke test confirms telemetry endpoint is not public beyond policy permission.

Summary: 0.6 Set up design foundations, application shells and API mocks
Description:
As a frontend developer,
I want approved design foundations and runnable public/admin application shells backed by API mocks,
So that UI stories can be developed consistently before all backend features are available.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Current UX contract
**When** Figma foundations and frontend theme are set up
**Then** color, typography, spacing, radius, elevation and motion tokens have unified semantic names
**And** the mapping between Figma tokens and code tokens is documented
**And** basic contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

**Given** the user opens the Public Portal shell
**When** navigate between `/`, `/explore`, `/map`, `/chat` and `/preferences`
**Then** the routes have shared heritage-storytelling navigation/layout and appropriate placeholder state
**And** desktop/mobile keep the same hierarchy
**And** the shell doesn't pretend to provide a feature that hasn't been implemented yet.

**Given** admin has entered the `/admin/*` shell
**When** navigates between placeholder admin areas
**Then** the interface uses Ant Design dashboard/form/table conventions instead of Tapestry composition
**And** public and admin themes do not leak styles or layouts to each other
**And** route structure is ready for auth guard in Story 1.1.

**Given** OpenAPI contract or response schema is defined
**When** the frontend calls the mock API
**Then** mock returns the correct schema response for representative success, empty and error cases
**And** the frontend uses generated/shared types instead of declaring duplicate payloads
**And** contract drift can be detected by automated checks.

**Given** a page is loading, has no data or has an error
**When** the shell renders the corresponding state
**Then** has reusable loading, empty and error primitives
**And** focus, keyboard navigation, landmark and accessible name basically work
**And** states are not only distinguished by color.

**Given** frontend shell can be run locally or on staging
**When** perform smoke test in representative desktop and mobile viewports
**Then** navigation and route rendering work without unintended horizontal overflow
**And** the frontend can switch between mock base URL and FastAPI base URL using environment configuration
**And** there is no need to edit the source code to change the environment.

Summary: 0.7 Set up test harness, fixtures and documentation templates
Description:
As a developer,
I want reusable automated test infrastructure and documentation templates,
So that every later story can prove its behavior and leave consistent implementation evidence.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** backend code needs unit, database or integration testing
**When** developer runs test suite according to documented command
**Then** pytest discovery, markers and test configuration work consistently locally/CI
**And** test database is isolated and reset between appropriate tests
**And** test does not depend on credential or shared staging data.

**Given** story needs representative knowledge data
**When** test uses fixture/factory
**Then** fixture has a minimum document, passage, entity and provenance with a defined ID
**And** can be extended to draft/published/version-isolation cases
**And** expected result is determined independently of the implementation under test.

**Given** frontend and API contract need testing
**When** contract test runs
**Then** representative success, validation error and service error payload are tested against the current schema
**And** mismatch between generated frontend types/mock and OpenAPI causes the test to fail.

**Given** Public/Admin shell runs with mock or test backend
**When** Playwright smoke suite runs
**Then** the suite tests the main route, navigation and a representative desktop/mobile viewport
**And** save screenshot/trace on failure
**And** selector prioritizes role/accessible names instead of fragile CSS structure dependencies.

**Given** AI/retrieval behavior is added in later epics
**When** developers add regression cases
**Then** harness supports fixed query, versioned evidence and deterministic expected gate/result
**And** report has room to record model, prompt, corpus and evaluation dataset version
**And** a test is not considered a pass just because the request did not crash.

**Given** a story that changes the API, database, operations or architecture
**When** story is completed
**Then** there are suitable templates for API/data docs, migration/rollback notes, ADR or runbooks
**And** test evidence and demo evidence have consistent location/link conventions
**And** the documentation does not require copying the same source of truth into multiple places.

**Given** Jenkins pipeline from Story 0.4
**When** test harness is integrated
**Then** unit, integration, contract and Playwright smoke checks run at the appropriate stage
**And** failure artifact is kept for diagnostics
**And** required test failure blocks deployment.

Summary: Epic 1: Admin Knowledge Studio
Description: Administrators log in and compile an entire knowledge package — document, passage, entity/alias/place profile, claim, timeline, relation, narrative and evidence — in draft state without manual SQL, UUID or foreign key manipulation.

Summary: 1.1 Authenticate, authorize and audit for Admin
Description:
As an administrator,
I want to sign in securely and have administrative actions authorized and audited,
So that only permitted users can modify cultural knowledge and every change is accountable.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a properly provisioned Admin account
**When** Admin logs in with correct information
**Then** the password is checked using Argon2id
**And** sessions are issued via cookies `HttpOnly`, `Secure` on staging/production and `SameSite` accordingly
**And** the raw password or session token does not appear in the response body, log or trace.

**Given** Incorrect credential or account not allowed to log in
**When** sends login request
**Then** the system refuses with a message not revealing which email/account exists
**And** does not create an authenticated session
**And** failure events are logged sufficiently for investigation but do not contain passwords, tokens, or raw IPs.

**Given** request to `/admin/*` or Admin API
**When** request does not have a valid session or does not have the necessary permissions
**Then** The UI moves to login or displays access-denied accordingly
**And** API returns `401` for unauthenticated or `403` for unauthorized
**And** does not perform partial write.

**Given** Admin has logged in
**When** session expires or Admin logs out
**Then** cookie/session is no longer available
**And** protected API denies further requests
**And** logging out multiple times does not cause unexpected errors.

**Given** an authenticated Admin to create, update, submit, review or publish action
**When** service transaction processes the action
**Then** audit record stores actor, action, target kind/ID, timestamp and correlation ID
**And** audit records cannot be edited/deleted via regular Admin CRUD
**And** failed transaction does not leave a false business success status.

**Given** login and authorization foundation tested
**When** run unit/integration/contract tests
**Then** test distinguishes success, invalid credentials, expired session, `401` and `403`
**And** test proves that unauthenticated write does not change the database
**And** audit output does not contain secrets or prohibited sensitive data.

Summary: 1.2 Create and manage source documents in draft state
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to create and manage source documents with complete provenance metadata,
So that cultural knowledge starts from a traceable source without direct database operations.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin opens the Document wizard
**When** creates source document
**Then** form collects source URL, title, region, source type, source tier, observed date, license and raw text/file according to contract
**And** required fields, URL/date/type constraints are displayed in the correct fields
**And** The UI does not require manual UUID or foreign key entry.

**Given** valid payload
**When** Admin saves the document
**Then** FastAPI/service transaction creates the document in the current draft corpus revision
**And** the default document has status `draft`, not `published`
**And** document does not appear in online serving query
**And** audit record is recorded for the create operation.

**Given** URL/content hash or metadata matches existing document
**When** Admin saves the draft
**Then** exact duplicate is blocked according to business constraints
**And** response specifies the duplicate field/candidate so that the Admin can edit or open the existing record
**And** does not create a second document or a garbage object.

**Given** raw document/file is stored on S3
**When** database write or object write fails
**Then** the system does not report successful saving
**And** does not leave a database row pointing to a non-existent object
**And** the orphan object is rolled back or marked for reconciliation according to the documented policy.

**Given** Admin finds or opens the draft document
**When** see list/details
**Then** can filter/search by title, region, source type and status
**And** metadata, raw-content availability and provenance are displayed
**And** loading, empty and error states have accessible behavior.

**Given** the document is still in draft revision and has not been submitted/published
**When** Admin updates or deletes document
**Then** change validation and execute atomically
**And** dependent-record conflicts are reported instead of being orphaned
**And** audit saves necessary before/after metadata.

**Given** document is in published release
**When** Admin tries to edit or delete published evidence
**Then** the system rejects direct mutations
**And** instructs Admin to create new revision/draft instead of changing historical evidence.

Summary: 1.3 Create a passage and select evidence directly from the source
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to create passages from a draft document and select them as evidence visually,
So that downstream knowledge records can cite exact source text without manual IDs.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a draft source document with raw text
**When** Admin opens the Passage workspace
**Then** raw text and passage list/preview are displayed in parallel
**And** passage is being highlighted correctly on raw text
**And** workspace supports keyboard navigation and does not just use color to indicate selection.

**Given** Admin selects a raw text or enters a valid char span
**When** creates passage
**Then** `char_start` and `char_end` are within the document
**And** passage content exactly matches the referenced substring according to the specified convention
**And** the system automatically generates the content hash and attaches the draft corpus revision
**And** Admin does not have to enter document UUID manually.

**Given** char span is empty, inverted, out of bounds, or content does not match raw text
**When** Admin saves passage
**Then** FastAPI rejects with error attaching correct field/span
**And** does not create partial passage or evidence record.

**Given** the passage has the same document, span or content hash that already exists in the revision
**When** Admin saves
**Then** exact duplicate is blocked
**And** UI leads to existing passage or allows adjustment of selection
**And** does not create duplicate records.

**Given** passage draft is valid
**When** Admin edits or deletes passage
**Then** the content hash/span is recalculated and validation runs within the transaction
**And** the system blocks deletion if the passage is being referenced by the knowledge record, and also lists dependencies
**And** audit record records the operation.

**Given** a form knowledge record that needs evidence in future stories
**When** Admin opens Evidence Picker
**Then** you can search for passages by document/title/text and select directly from the preview
**And** component returns a valid reference but does not require the user to enter a UUID/FK
**And** selected evidence displays the source title and excerpt for inspection.

**Given** passage is in published release
**When** Admin tries to edit content/span
**Then** the system rejects direct mutations
**And** requires creating a new revision so that the historical citation remains unchanged.

Summary: 1.4 Manage entities, aliases and place profiles
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to create and manage entities, aliases and place profiles with evidence,
So that cultural concepts are canonical, searchable and traceable before publication.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin opens Entity editor
**When** creates entity
**Then** form collects canonical name, normalized name, type, subtype, scope and status according to registry
**And** entities are attached to draft corpus revision and are not served online by default
**And** Admin does not have to manually enter corpus/entity UUID.

**Given** canonical/normalized name is the same or close to existing entity/alias
**When** Admin imports or saves entities
**Then** exact duplicate is blocked
**And** fuzzy candidates are displayed with name, type and region/context sufficient for comparison
**And** Admin can open candidate instead of accidentally creating duplicate entities.

**Given** entity draft already exists
**When** Admin adds, edits or deletes aliases
**Then** the alias is normalized consistently with the entity resolution contract
**And** Empty aliases, duplicates in the same entity, or invalid conflicts are explicitly rejected
**And** mutations are audited and executed atomically.

**Given** entity has type location
**When** Admin creates place profile
**Then** coordinates and geographical/administrative fields can be entered according to the schema
**And** latitude/longitude is tested for range and value pairs
**And** non-place entities cannot receive place profiles that are left of the constraint.

**Given** entities need provenance
**When** Admin uses Evidence Picker from Story 1.3
**Then** can choose primary evidence and one or more supporting passages
**And** evidence must be in a valid revision/context
**And** UI displays source title and excerpt, no passage ID required.

**Given** Admin finds entities to edit or link later
**When** searches by canonical name, alias, type or region
**Then** the result distinguishes canonical name from alias match
**And** draft/published status is clearly displayed
**And** loading, empty, duplicate-warning and error states support keyboard/screen reader.

**Given** entity draft is being referenced by another knowledge record
**When** Admin tries to delete entity
**Then** the system blocks orphan references and lists dependencies
**And** does not perform partial delete.

**Given** entity/alias/place profile is a published release
**When** Admin tries to edit directly
**Then** the system rejects mutation history
**And** directs Admin to create a new draft revision.

Summary: 1.5 Compile typed claims with evidence
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to author typed claims for an entity using a governing field registry,
So that factual attributes are validated, versioned and traceable to source passages.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin selects an entity draft and `claim_field`
**When** Claim form is displayed
**Then** control is generated according to `value_type`: `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `year`, `money` or `json`
**And** form displays `label_vi`, default unit and time-sensitive guidance
**And** Admin does not enter entity ID or field code manually.

**Given** Admin enters claim value
**When** value does not match the type of `claim_field`
**Then** UI/FastAPI reports an error in the field before or when saving
**And** database constraint/trigger still rejects invalid payloads if application validation is bypassed
**And** does not create partial claims.

**Given** a valid claim
**When** Admin does not enter units and fields with `default_unit`
**Then** default units are applied consistently
**And** units are displayed in the preview before saving.

**Given** Admin enters `observed_at`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, confidence and canonical state
**When** save claim
**Then** confidence only accepts between 0 and 1
**And** `valid_until` cannot be before `valid_from`
**And** time-sensitive claim requires contract time metadata
**And** claim is saved in state `draft`.

**Given** claim requires provenance
**When** Admin selects evidence
**Then** must have a primary passage and can have multiple supporting passages
**And** claim, entities and passages belong to the same valid draft corpus version
**And** source title/excerpt is displayed instead of UUID.

**Given** a claim with the same entity, field and value already exists in revision
**When** Admin saves
**Then** exact duplicate is blocked or redirected to an existing record
**And** canonical-state conflict is clearly warned
**And** do not create unintentional duplicate claims.

**Given** claim draft already exists
**When** Admin edits or deletes claim
**Then** type, validity, confidence and evidence are validated again in the transaction
**And** the operation is audited
**And** published claim cannot be edited directly but must create a new revision.

Summary: 1.6 Compile timeline events and participants
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to author evidence-backed timeline events with typed participant roles,
So that an entity's history can be presented and queried consistently.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin opens the Timeline editor for an entity
**When** creates event
**Then** form collects title, `year_start`, optional `year_end`, precision, event type, summary, actor and artifact according to the schema
**And** precision only accepts `year`, `decade`, `century`, `range` or `circa`
**And** event type is selected from the registry, no free code is entered.

**Given** Admin enters the timeline
**When** `year_end` is less than `year_start` or precision/range is invalid
**Then** UI and FastAPI report errors in the relevant field
**And** the database constraint still protects the year range
**And** does not create partial events.

**Given** event has participating individuals, organizations, locations or artifacts
**When** Admin adds participant
**Then** entities are searched/selected by canonical name or alias
**And** role is selected from `participant_role` registry
**And** and the same entity/role cannot be added to the same event
**And** Admin does not enter entity ID or role code manually.

**Given** Admin selects actor or artifact
**When** saves the event
**Then** reference must point to a valid entity in the corpus context
**And** type mismatch is clearly warned or rejected according to business rules
**And** deleted/invalid reference does not create an orphan relation.

**Given** timeline event needs provenance
**When** Admin selects evidence
**Then** must have a primary passage and can have supporting passages
**And** event and evidence belong to the same draft corpus version
**And** source title/excerpt is displayed in the editor.

**Given** equivalent event already exists for the same entity, time range, type and title
**When** Admin saves
**Then** exact duplicate is blocked or results in an existing event
**And** event at the same time but other content is allowed to exist and presented separately.

**Given** valid event and participant list
**When** Admin saves or updates
**Then** events, participants and evidence are atomically recorded in state `draft`
**And** the operation is audited
**And** failure in any part rolls back all changes.

**Given** timeline event is a published release
**When** Admin tries to edit or delete directly
**Then** the system rejects mutation history
**And** requires creating a new draft revision.

Summary: 1.7 Build typed entity relations
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to connect two entities with a governing predicate and supporting evidence,
So that graph relationships remain valid, explainable and queryable.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin opens the Relation builder
**When** select subject, predicate and object
**Then** The UI displays the structure `subject ─ predicate → object`
**And** subject/object is searched by canonical name or alias
**And** predicate is selected from the closed registry, no code or UUID entered manually.

**Given** predicate has `is_symmetric` or `inverse_of`
**When** Admin selects predicate
**Then** builder displays appropriate semantics/inverse for Admin to check relationship direction
**And** do not create inverse relations outside the specified contract.

**Given** subject and object are the same
**When** Admin saves the relation
**Then** UI, FastAPI and database refuse self-loop
**And** does not create partial relation/evidence.

**Given** the same subject, predicate, object and corpus version already exists
**When** Admin saves
**Then** exact triple duplicate is suppressed and the existing record is displayed
**And** does not silently merge different evidence or confidence.

**Given** Admin enters confidence and evidence
**When** saves relation
**Then** confidence only accepts from 0 to 1
**And** primary passage is required, supporting passages are optional
**And** relation, entities and passages belong to the same draft corpus context.

**Given** relation is valid
**When** Admin creates, updates or deletes
**Then** relation and evidence are atomically written in state `draft`
**And** the operation is audited
**And** published relation cannot be edited directly but must create a new revision.

Summary: 1.8 Compile narrative sections with evidence
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to compose ordered Markdown narrative sections for an entity with source evidence,
So that published heritage content can tell a coherent story without losing provenance.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin opens the Narrative editor for an entity
**When** create section
**Then** section code is selected from the allowed registry, including overview, name, origin, historical role, architecture, artifacts, characters, modern changes or tours
**And** form collects title, Markdown body and order index
**And** Admin does not enter entity ID or section code freely.

**Given** the same entity, section code and corpus version already have sections
**When** Admin creates more
**Then** exact section duplicates are blocked and the existing section is opened for editing
**And** other sections of code are still allowed to exist.

**Given** Admin composes Markdown
**When** opens preview
**Then** headings, lists, links and emphasis are rendered consistent with the public content contract
**And** unsafe HTML/script is sanitized
**And** editor/preview is keyboard-enabled and has accessible labels.

**Given** narrative section needs provenance
**When** Admin selects evidence
**Then** a primary passage is required and supporting passages can be multiple
**And** selected sources shows title/excerpt instead of UUID
**And** section and evidence belong to the same draft corpus version.

**Given** Admin changes order index or content
**When** save narrative package
**Then** ordering, Markdown and evidence are validated and recorded atomically
**And** section defaults to state `draft`
**And** the operation is audited.

**Given** the narrative section is a published release
**When** Admin tries to edit or delete directly
**Then** the system rejects mutation history
**And** requires creating a new revision draft.

Summary: Epic 2: Reliable Corpus Validation and Publishing
Description: Editors submit drafts to Airflow for deep validation, generate embeddings, indexes, and manifests, resolve issues, conduct reviews, and publish corpus releases atomically. A dashboard shows the health and publication readiness of each release.

Summary: 2.1 Submit draft revision and create validation run idempotent
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to submit a draft corpus revision for asynchronous validation,
So that deep validation runs once per logical submission without blocking normal authoring saves.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an authenticated Admin with draft revision
**When** Admin selects Submit for Validation
**Then** FastAPI performs minimal preflight checks on revision, ownership/status and required package records
**And** saving normally does not automatically trigger Airflow
**And** submission does not make the draft published.

**Given** valid submission with new idempotency key
**When** service processes the request
**Then** the validation run is created atomically with revision ID, requester, timestamps and initial state
**And** run ID is immediately returned to the UI for asynchronous tracking
**And** the operation is audited.

**Given** the same revision and idempotency key are sent back
**When** request retry due to timeout or network failure
**Then** service returns an existing validation run
**And** does not create a second run or DAG execution.

**Given** idempotency key is already used for another revision/payload
**When** the client reuses the key
**Then** The API returns an explicit conflict
**And** does not change the existing run.

**Given** multiple requests submitted at the same time with the same revision
**When** service handles concurrency
**Then** database uniqueness/transaction ensures that only one logical run is created
**And** the remaining requests receive the same run or conflict.

**Given** validation run has been committed
**When** Airflow trigger is successful
**Then** run saves the external DAG/run reference and enters the appropriate queued/running state
**And** correlation ID connects API submission to Airflow execution.

**Given** Airflow trigger failed after run was created
**When** service logs an error
**Then** run has an explicit retryable/trigger-failed status
**And** retry reuses the same logical run instead of creating a new run
**And** The UI does not indicate that validation is running if the DAG has not been triggered.

**Given** revision changes after a submission
**When** Admin wants to review new content
**Then** must create a new submission/version identity
**And** the old run's report still properly references the audited snapshot/revision.

Summary: 2.2 Run Airflow deep validation and record validation issues
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want the knowledge submitted package to be checked deeply with actionable issues,
So that I can correct invalid or incomplete records before indexes or a release is prepared.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** revision validation run has been triggered for a snapshot
**When** Airflow starts deep validation
**Then** pipeline only reads data belonging to the submitted snapshot/revision
**And** the current status and start/end time of each stage are recorded
**And** changing the draft later does not change the results of the currently running run.

**Given** package contains document, passage, entity, claim, timeline, relation and narrative
**When** validation stages run
**Then** the system checks required fields, type/range, foreign key, exact duplicate, provenance and corpus-version consistency
**And** business constraints of each record type are checked
**And** the quality blocking error is classified as `error`, the issue needing review is classified as `warning`.

**Given** a validation rule that detects the problem
**When** issue is recorded
**Then** issue contains run, stage, severity, rule/code, record kind/ID, field/path and actionable messages
**And** The UI has enough references to open the correct record that needs editing
**And** issue does not require Admin to read Airflow log to identify error objects.

**Given** the same run/stage is retried
The **When** pipeline logs the results
**Then** issues are upsert/reconcile to a stable identity
**And** does not create duplicate issues just because of a retry
**And** issues that are no longer valid after the retest are marked resolved or replaced according to policy.

**Given** a stage validation failed due to an operator error
**When** run stops
**Then** run is not marked as passable
**And** stage errors, safety messages and recorded results are retained for diagnostics
**And** retry continues safely without creating a new logical run.

**Given** validation has any unresolved `error`
**When** the pipeline is about to move to embedding/indexing or publishing
**Then** the following step is blocked
**And** warnings are displayed for review but do not automatically turn into pass/fail outside of the specified policy.

**Given** validation completed
**When** Admin views summary
**Then** the total number of errors/warnings and results by stage match the issue records
**And** metrics/logs/traces are linked by validation run/correlation ID
**And** Airflow does not have the right to publish the corpus itself.

Summary: 2.3 Create embeddings, indexes and reproducible manifest
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want every validated revision prepared as one reproducible serving package,
So that search, graph and chatbot components can use consistent artifacts after publication.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** validation run completed and there are no more blocking errors
**When** the preparation pipeline starts
**Then** passages are divided into semantic chunks according to the versioned chunking contract
**And** each chunk has a stable ID, source passage reference and content hash
**And** together with input/configuration recreates the same chunk identities.

**Given** chunks need vector embedding
**When** the embedding stage runs
**Then** model, model version and vector dimension match the embedding contract
**And** vectors with wrong dimensions are rejected instead of being written to the index
**And** constant chunks can reuse artifacts according to content hash and contract version.

**Given** validated records and chunks are ready
**When** indexing stages run
**Then** lexical, accent-insensitive/trigram, vector and graph projection artifacts are all attached to the corpus revision
**And** artifacts are recorded in the staging namespace, not yet used by online consumers
**And** partial artifacts are not marked ready.

**Given** all preparation stages are successful
**When** pipeline creates manifest
**Then** manifest records corpus revision, chunk IDs/hashes, embedding contract, index versions, graph projection version, record counts and artifact checksums/locations
**And** manifest is saved with version on S3
**And** secrets or private infrastructure credentials do not appear in the manifest.

**Given** the same revision/configuration is retried
**When** pipeline records chunks, embeddings, indexes or manifest
**Then** writes is idempotent or reconciled according to deterministic artifact identity
**And** does not generate duplicate serving packages
**And** stale/partial artifacts are replaced or cleaned up according to documented policy.

**Given** any preparation stage or manifest verification fails
**When** run ends
**Then** release is not marked publish-ready
**And** active published artifacts are currently unchanged
**And** stage/error is recorded for retry and observation.

Summary: 2.4 Monitor Validation Center, fix errors and resubmit
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to see validation progress and navigate directly to records that need correction,
So that I can repair a failed package and submit a clean revision without reading infrastructure logs.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin opens Validation Center
**When** has validation runs
**Then** the list displays revision, run status, current stage, time, error count and warning count
**And** queued, running, failed, passed and retryable states are distinguished by text/icon, not just color
**And** loading, empty, stale and service-error states are clearly displayed.

**Given** a run has issues
**When** Admin opens quality report
**Then** can filter by severity, stage, record type and rule
**And** each issue displays the message, field/path, available source context, and current status
**And** shows the total number of matches for run's issue records.

**Given** issue references a knowledge record
**When** Admin selects Fix/Open
**Then** UI opens the correct editor and record to be edited
**And** keeps the context of run/issue so Admin can return to report
**And** Admin does not have to copy UUID or look up the database.

**Given** run failed because of an operation error and the snapshot remained unchanged
**When** Admin selects Retry
**Then** system retry with safe logical run/snapshot
**And** do not create duplicate issues/artifacts
**And** action and results are audited.

**Given** Admin has edited the knowledge content
**When** select Resubmit
**Then** the system creates a new submission/run for the new snapshot revision
**And** the old report remains unchanged for comparison
**And** UI shows which issues have been resolved, still exist, or have just appeared according to rule/record identity.

**Given** Admin does not have validation/retry/resubmit rights
**When** tries to perform action
**Then** API/UI refuses to match
**And** does not trigger Airflow or run changes.

Summary: 2.5 Human review and atomic corpus publication
Description:
As a human reviewer,
I want to inspect a validated release and explicitly approve or reject it before atomic publication,
So that unreviewed or partially activated knowledge never reaches users.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** release candidate has validation pass and serving package ready
**When** Reviewer opens the Review workspace
**Then** workspace displays revision diff, provenance summary, warnings, conflicting sources, manifest/index status and validation history
**And** Reviewer can go to the related record/evidence
**And** draft data is not displayed as published.

**Given** candidate still has blocking error, preparation not ready or manifest is invalid
**When** Reviewer tries to approve/publish
**Then** action is blocked with failed gate list
**And** Airflow password is fake or the warning is changed to an out-of-policy password that cannot bypass the gate.

**Given** Reviewer decided to reject
**When** enter the reason and confirm
**Then** candidate keeps the unpublished status
**And** decision, reviewer, timestamp and note are audited
**And** the current active release remains unchanged.

**Given** Reviewer approves a qualified candidate
**When** open Publish confirmation
**Then** The UI displays the release/version to be activated, the gates passed, the manifest artifact and the rollback/retire path
**And** publish only continues after explicit confirmation
**And** Airflow does not directly call publish.

**Given** publication confirmed
**When** Publishing Service activate release
**Then** database transaction ensures the new release becomes active and the previous release is changed status according to the policy as a consistent operation
**And** online release/artifact pointer only switches to verified serving package
**And** publish event, reviewer and manifest identity are audited.

**Given** transaction, artifact activation or concurrent publish encountered an error
**When** publish was not fully completed
**Then** online consumers continue to use the most recent good release
**And** there is no new database state but the old index is considered the same release
**And** errors/conflicts are clearly reported for retry or review.

Summary: 2.6 Ensure published corpus version isolation
Description:
As an end user,
I want each request to use one complete published corpus version,
So that pages, recommendations and chatbot answers never mix old and new knowledge.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an online request started
**When** service resolve active release
**Then** release ID is retained for the entire request lifecycle
**And** database, lexical/vector indexes, graph projection and evidence queries all use that release
**And** response/trace records the appropriate release ID.

**Given** the new release is published while the old request is running
**When** the old request continues retrieval or persistence
**Then** request still completes on the pinned release
**And** new requests can use new releases
**And** do not mix artifacts of two releases.

**Given** records have the status of draft, retired, withdrawn or belong to another release
**When** online consumers query
**Then** record does not appear in the serving results of active release
**And** the repository/service boundary applies the filter instead of depending on the endpoint to remember the filter itself.

**Given** a required artifact of the pinned release is missing or the checksum/version does not match
**When** request needs that artifact
**Then** the service returns the appropriate unavailable/degraded status instead of silently falling back to another release
**And** does not generate answers, citations or recommendations from mixed versions
**And** failures are measured and traced.

**Given** response fact is saved or returned
**When** the system records evidence/citation
**Then** corpus release ID is saved with response/evidence
**And** the cited passage of the published release remains unchanged to trace history.

**Given** version isolation tested
**When** run concurrent publish and online-request integration tests
**Then** tests demonstrate no draft leakage or cross-version reads
**And** expected values checks for the correct record/version, not just checks that the request does not crash.

Summary: 2.7 Display corpus health and publish readiness dashboard
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want one dashboard showing corpus, validation, index and evaluation health,
So that I can know whether the current draft and published releases are safe and ready to serve.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin opens the dashboard
**When** operating data is available
**Then** the dashboard displays current draft release, active published release, validation queue, issue counts, review status and publish eligibility
**And** each state has timestamp/freshness
**And** stale or unavailable data is not presented as healthy.

**Given** corpus health data available
**When** dashboard renders
**Then** displays record counts by type/status, provenance gaps, duplicate/quality summary and graph coverage as appropriate
**And** metrics link to actionable reports or filtered records
**And** dashboards do not auto-correct data.

**Given** serving artifacts have been prepared or published
**When** see index/model health
**Then** dashboard displays manifest identity, lexical/vector/graph status, embedding/model contract, prompt/related model version and last successful build
**And** artifact/release mismatch is clearly marked blocking or degraded.

**Given** evaluation reports exist
**When** dashboard displays quality metrics
**Then** citation faithfulness, citation coverage, abstention accuracy, retrieval recall and latency are tied to model, prompt, corpus and dataset versions
**And** missing metrics are not displayed as reaching target.

**Given** a validation, pipeline, index or publish gate error
**When** operator views dashboard or alert
**Then** has a link to the relevant run/release/correlation ID
**And** Prometheus/Grafana/Langfuse signals support diagnostics instead of replacing source-of-truth status
**And** sensitive content, password, token and raw IP do not appear.

**Given** the user does not have administrative rights
**When** access API/UI dashboard
**Then** access is denied accordingly
**And** corpus operational details are not exposed to the public surface.

**Given** the component library and Admin Console handoff from Stories 0.8–0.9 plus the Admin shell from Story 0.6
**When** FE implements `/admin`
**Then** layout, typography, spacing, components and responsive behavior follow the approved Figma design
**And** FE uses shared/generated API types instead of hard-coding production metrics
**And** visual deviations are approved by DES or recorded.

**Given** the dashboard is loading, has no data, partially fails or fails completely
**When** the UI renders the corresponding state
**Then** loading skeletons, empty guidance, partial-data warnings and retryable error states appear at the correct scope
**And** one failed widget does not cause a blank dashboard
**And** status is not communicated by color alone.

**Given** desktop, tablet and minimum supported viewports
**When** component and Playwright tests plus design QA run
**Then** the dashboard has no unintended horizontal overflow
**And** keyboard navigation, landmarks and focus order work
**And** DES compares representative rendered states with Figma before the story is marked done.

Summary: Epic 3: Heritage Discovery and Storytelling Portal
Description: Users find and select published heritage content through Home, Explore/Library, the 2D Hue–Da Nang map, and Content Landing. From there, they can continue to scene experiences, Chat, Recommendations, or related content when those capabilities are available.

Summary: 3.1 Explore featured heritage experiences
Description:
As a visitor,
I want to featured browse heritage experiences from the public home page,
So that I can quickly choose a place or story to explore without knowing what to search for first.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the user opens the Home page
**When** active published corpus has featured content
**Then** page displays featured content groups according to editorial configuration
**And** all cards belong to the same published corpus release pin
**And** drafts, withdrawn or content belonging to another release do not appear.

**Given** an experience card is displayed
**When** the user views the card
**Then** cards prioritize images and experience names, not stuffing timelines, sources or long descriptions
**And** there are two obvious actions to continue exploring and open Content Landing
**And** button/link has a clear accessible name and keyboard focus.

**Given** the user chooses the discovery action
**When** navigates to Explore
**Then** appropriate context such as region, topic, or content type is passed through the shareable URL/state
**And** back navigation takes the user to the correct location on Home.

**Given** the user chooses to open the content
**When** Content Landing exists in the current release
**Then** navigate to the correct content slug/ID
**And** do not use mocks or data from other releases.

**Given** card image not loaded, error or out of viewport
**When** Home renders
**Then** images use responsive sizes, placeholders/fallbacks, and appropriate lazy loading
**And** image errors do not cause the card or navigation to become unavailable
**And** layout does not jump abnormally when the image is complete.

**Given** Home has no featured content or API errors
**When** the page loads
**Then** displays the empty/error state with a clear path forward
**And** does not display blank pages or draft data as fallback.

Summary: 3.2 Search and filter the heritage content library
Description:
As a visitor,
I want to search and filter the published heritage library,
So that I can find experiences relevant to a name, region or cultural category.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the user opens Explore/Library
**When** has not entered the condition
**Then** the page displays published experiences with specified pagination or incremental loading
**And** card uses the same visual/action contract as Home
**And** do not load the entire media or the entire corpus at once.

**Given** the user enters a keyword
**When** perform a search
**Then** the system searches published content by standard name and appropriate alias
**And** the query is normalized according to the search contract
**And** the results do not call Qwen just to rank the Explore list.

**Given** the user selects region or category filters
**When** apply individually or in combination
**Then** the result contains only records that satisfy all active filters
**And** supports at least Hue, Da Nang and content groups within the project scope
**And** filter state is shown in the URL to reload/share without losing options.

**Given** query/filter returned no results
**When** search completed
**Then** the page displays the empty state, the conditions being applied, and how to delete/edit the conditions
**And** does not replace itself with unrelated results or draft content.

**Given** request is slow, error or out of page
**When** Explore updates results
**Then** loading, retry, end-of-results and stale-result states are clearly distinguished
**And** keyboard/screen reader receives result change notification
**And** the old card is not mistakenly attached to the new query.

Summary: 3.3 Explore locations on the 2D Hue–Da Nang map
Description:
As a visitor,
I want to discover published heritage experiences on a two-dimensional map,
So that I can understand where places are located and begin a geographically grounded experience.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** user opens `/map`
**When** the overview map loads
**Then** shows 2D Vietnam map, not globe or 3D earth
**And** Hue and Da Nang are represented by two highlighted points/areas
**And** animation respects reduced-motion preference.

**Given** users choose Hue or Da Nang
**When** the map switches to regional view
**Then** displays published places markers with valid coordinates in that area
**And** marker belongs to the same pinned corpus release
**And** content that is missing or has wrong coordinates cannot be placed at fake locations.

**Given** the user selects the marker
**When** place preview opens
**Then** preview displays the image, name, and actions to explore/open the Content Landing under the same contract as the card
**And** indicates an active preview that is explicitly linked to the currently selected marker
**And** closes the preview and returns focus to the marker.

**Given** the user cannot or does not want to manipulate the map directly
**When** use keyboard, screen reader or select list view
**Then** has a list of locations that are equivalent in content and action
**And** select in the list to synchronize with the corresponding marker
**And** map is not the only way to access content.

**Given** viewport mobile
**When** the user selects an area or marker
**Then** the preview/list displayed using the layout or bottom sheet does not obscure the entire context
**And** close, scroll and focus operations work clearly.

**Given** map tiles/data error
**When** map fails to render
**Then** the Hue–Da Nang location list is still active
**And** does not display a blank page or block the path to Content Landing.

Summary: 3.4 View Content Landing before starting a scene experience
Description:
As a visitor,
I want to review the identity and context of a heritage experience before starting it,
So that I understand what I am about to explore and can choose my next action.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the user opens a valid Content Landing
**When** content belongs to active published release
**Then** the page displays the appropriate profile picture, name, subtitle/short description, region, content type and provenance/partner information
**And** response and trace attached to pinned corpus release
**And** does not display draft or mixed-version data.

**Given** content with scene experience published and available
**When** the landing page renders
**Then** the `Start Experience` action is displayed according to the published scene capability/route contract
**And** the landing does not automatically load the 3D model, audio, or entire scene assets before the user starts it.

**Given** scene experience is not available yet
**When** the landing page renders
**Then** the page still provides introductory information, sources, and related content
**And** does not show dead links or pretend that the experience is ready
**And** availability status is clearly expressed.

**Given** content has related published experiences
**When** the user views the relevant section
**Then** can continue to another Content Landing or Explore appropriate context
**And** related links do not point to draft/withdrawn records
**And** back navigation retains the previous journey.

**Given** hero image or media preview error
**When** the page renders
**Then** fallback image/state is displayed but title, description, provenance and navigation still work
**And** not loading 3D/audio causes automatic fallback.

**Given** content does not exist in pinned release
**When** route is opened
**Then** displays the not-found state with a path back to Home, Explore or Map
**And** does not fallback to the same ID in another draft or release.

**Given** Content Landing is measured in the target environment
**When** representative published content is downloaded
**Then** meets the detailed page load budget of ≤3 seconds under recorded measurement conditions
**And** desktop/mobile maintains hierarchy, focus order and no unwanted horizontal overflow.

Summary: Epic 4: Grounded Q&A Assistant
Description: Users ask questions in Vietnamese from the Chat page or the panel beside Content. The system identifies the correct entity and intent, retrieves evidence from a published corpus release, uses Qwen3-4B to formulate the response, and returns only `answered`, `clarify`, or `abstained` after validating citations and grounding.

Summary: 4.1 Understand the question and identify the correct entity
Description:
As a user,
I want the assistant to understand Vietnamese names, aliases and typing variations,
So that my question is connected to the correct heritage entity or I am asked to clarify.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** user sent a question in Vietnamese
**When** query understanding begins
**Then** the system keeps the raw query intact and creates a normalized query according to the contract
**And** consistently handles uppercase/lowercase letters, Vietnamese accents, spaces, and character variations
**And** normalization does not cause loss of raw text that needs to be displayed or audited.

**Given** the question contains the canonical name or reviewed alias
**When** entity resolution runs
**Then** canonical name exact, normalized alias exact and accent-insensitive match are prioritized in the specified order
**And** typo/fuzzy matching is only used within calibrated thresholds
**And** only entities belonging to pinned published release and `in_scope` will be selected to reply.

**Given** has exactly one candidate who exceeds the confidence threshold
**When** resolver completes
**Then** returns entity ID/canonical name along with traceable match reason
**And** context hints from Content Landing are checked and do not automatically override the question content.

**Given** has many reasonable candidates or the names are not distinctive enough
**When** resolver cannot be safely selected
**Then** terminal result is `clarify`
**And** response provides brief options with distinguishing information such as type or region
**And** the system does not randomly select an entity.

**Given** the question does not need a specific entity or no entity was found
**When** resolver completes
**Then** the contract clearly states `entity_ids`, `needs_clarification` and scope status
**And** valid generic queries can proceed
**And** entities outside the scope cannot be assumed to be entities in the corpus.

**Given** resolver is tested
**When** it runs cases with canonical names, aliases, unaccented text, typing errors, duplicate names, and out-of-scope entities
**Then** expected entity/clarify outcome is specifically verified
**And** test is not just checking that the request does not crash.

Summary: 4.2 Determine intent and plan to find evidence
Description:
As a user,
I want the assistant to recognize what kind of answer I need,
So that it looks in the right knowledge structures instead of applying one generic search to every question.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** query has normalized and entity resolution is complete or no entity is needed
**When** the intent router runs
**Then** sort into one of `overview`, `field`, `timeline`, `relationship`, `section`, `comparison`, `open_text` or `out_of_scope`
**And** output records confidence/reason suitable for tracing
**And** cases below the threshold are clarified or handled according to the specified fallback.

**Given** query contains an identifiable field, time period, or relation request
**When** router creates structured query contract
**Then** contract fill in `field_code`, `time_range` or `requested_relations` as appropriate
**And** does not invent fields/predicates outside of the registry.

**Given** intent identified
**When** Query Planner plans
**Then** the planner selects a small, predefined list of operators that match the intent
**And** plan records input, limit/budget and the order in which operators need to run
**And** planner does not generate free SQL or act as an autonomous agent.

**Given** comparative questions or need many types of evidence
**When** planner creates multi-operator plan
**Then** the necessary branches of evidence are clearly stated and pinned together in a corpus release
**And** duplicate operators are not run merely because the same data appears in multiple branches.

**Given** intent is `out_of_scope`
**When** planning is complete
**Then** the system does not run unnecessarily expensive retrieval/generation
**And** returns the appropriate status, don't make up an out-of-scope answer.

**Given** router/planner tested
**When** runs representative questions for eight intents
**Then** expected intent, fields and operator plan are compared to the gold set
**And** change the prompt/rule to deviate the plan detected by regression tests.

Summary: 4.3 Find evidence from facts, timeline, graph, narrative and text
Description:
As a user,
I want the assistant to retrieve evidence that matches my question,
So that answers are based on the most appropriate published knowledge rather than model memory.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** plan requires exact facts
**When** Exact operator runs
**Then** get the claim/canonical value appropriate to the entity, field, validity and pinned release
**And** returns supporting passage references
**And** stale/time-sensitive value is not represented as current outside the validity contract.

**Given** plan requires events or chronology
**When** Timeline operator runs
**Then** filter timeline events by appropriate entity, event type and time range
**And** keeps actor/participant/artifact with evidence
**And** sorts according to specified time semantics.

**Given** plan requires relationship
**When** Graph operator runs
**Then** traversal limits 1–2 hops through the predicate allowlist that matches the intent
**And** every node/edge belongs to the same pinned published release
**And** path and supporting passages are returned to explain the results.

**Given** plan requires topical content
**When** Section operator runs
**Then** get the narrative sections with the correct entity/section intent and associated evidence
**And** do not replace the reviewed narrative with an unsourced model-generated summary.

**Given** plan requires searching in text or paraphrase
**When** Text operator runs
**Then** combines PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm/accent-insensitive search and vector channel according to contract
**And** the results are consolidated according to the published ranking method
**And** vector dimension/model must match the pinned release manifest.

**Given** an operator with insufficient results or a dependency error
**When** retrieval ends
**Then** trace records operator, candidate counts, ranks and failure/degradation
**And** does not fallback to another draft or corpus release
**And** downstream receives clearly empty/missing evidence instead of fabricated data.

Summary: 4.4 Build evidence package and block questions lacking evidence
Description:
As a user,
I want the assistant to answer only when it has enough relevant evidence,
So that confident wording is not produced from weak, mismatched or conflicting sources.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** retrieval operators return candidates
**When** Entity Dossier/Evidence Context Builder runs
**Then** merge claims, events, relations, narratives and passages that match the intent
**And** type duplicate evidence according to stable identity/content
**And** retains conflicting sources instead of silently choosing one.

**Given** evidence exceeds context budget
**When** builder selects evidence
**Then** applies the configuration budget according to intent and prioritizes provenance/relevance
**And** does not limit the old Text operator as invariant to the entire system
**And** selection order and reason can be traced.

**Given** evidence is included in package
**When** package is complete
**Then** each item has a stable citation ID in the request, source/passage reference and corpus release ID
**And** model only sees citation IDs belonging to package
**And** evidence text is considered data, not instructions that have the power to change system behavior.

**Given** pre-generation gate runs
**When** entity/scope, publish status, freshness, release consistency or evidence threshold are not met
**Then** Qwen is not called
**And** the result is `clarify` if the user can clarify, or `abstained` if the evidence is insufficient
**And** the gate reason is saved for trace/evaluation.

**Given** evidence is sufficient and consistent according to policy
**When** pre-generation gate pass
**Then** package only contains evidence of a pinned release
**And** generation request receives bounded package with prompt/model version
**And** package can be saved/reproduced for regression investigation.

Summary: 4.5 Generate and check answers with citations
Description:
As a user,
I want a clear Vietnamese answer whose factual claims are supported by visible citations,
So that I can trust the response or understand when the system cannot answer.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** pre-generation gate has passed
**When** Qwen3-4B receives generation request
**Then** model only accepts query, structured context and bounded evidence package
**And** does not have permission to query the database, create entities/relation/sources, or add facts from model memory
**And** output follows the response schema and citation IDs provided.

**Given** evidence proves that the question premise is wrong
**When** model generates response
**Then** the answer corrects the premise right at the beginning
**And** correction with supporting citation
**And** does not repeat a false premise as a fact.

**Given** generation completed
**When** post-generation gate runs
**Then** check the citation IDs belonging to the package, factual claims have support, number/date matches evidence, certainty matches and conflict is presented
**And** citation does not exist or claim is not supported causing gate failure
**And** output is not returned as `answered` just because it is in a valid format.

**Given** grounding fails but the error can be fixed with a regeneration
**When** retry policy allows
**Then** the system retries at most once with fail-safe feedback
**And** if it still fails, returns `abstained`
**And** does not loop infinitely or bypass gates.

**Given** model timeout or unavailable
**When** request could not be completed
**Then** returns a friendly error/abstained status, not a fabricated fallback answer
**And** the current evidence/release has not been changed
**And** failures are measured and traced.

**Given** response completed
**When** saves and returns results
**Then** terminal status is just `answered`, `clarify` or `abstained`
**And** save query, pinned release, evidence references, model/prompt version, grounding result and latency according to privacy policy
**And** `answered` always has valid citations for factual content.

Summary: 4.6 Use Chat independently and alongside Content
Description:
As a user,
I want to ask questions either from a dedicated Chat page or aside the content I am viewing,
So that I can get grounded help without losing my exploration context.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** user opens `/chat`
**When** starts conversation
**Then** can submit questions in Vietnamese without logging in
**And** UI clearly displays sending, answered, clarified, abstained and service error status
**And** conversation does not assume an entity context if the user has not selected it.

**Given** the user opens Chat from Content Landing
**When** the contextual panel appears
**Then** The UI displays the chip/label for the entity in question
**And** sends the entity ID as a context hint to be verified by the backend on the pinned release
**And** users can remove or change explicit context, there is no hidden context.

**Given** desktop viewport is wide enough
**When** Chat panel opens next to Content
**Then** Content and Chat are displayed side by side without covering the main controls/content
**And** the panel can be collapsed/reopened
**And** loading or Chat errors do not stop Content Landing from working.

**Given** mobile or narrow viewport
**When** the user selects `Ask AI`
**Then** Chat opens with drawer/bottom sheet or full-screen panel with clear close/back
**And** closes the Chat and returns the user to the correct Content location
**And** focus is managed and background interaction is limited accordingly.

**Given** the assistant returns `answered`
**When** response rendered
**Then** citations are controls that have an accessible label and open source/excerpt accordingly
**And** number/date/source formatting is easy to read
**And** citation clicking does not cause unwanted conversation loss.

**Given** the assistant returns `clarify` or `abstained`
**When** response rendered
**Then** The UI explains what the user needs to clarify or why the evidence is not enough
**And** provides the appropriate next action without presenting it as a general technical error
**And** does not display answer text that does not pass through the gate.

**Given** contextual Chat component is composed in a representative host using a public integration contract
**When** host transmits scene/entity context
**Then** component reuses the same Chat implementation, does not require a second chatbot
**And** context is displayed transparently before submitting the question
**And** the contract has an automated component/contract test so hosts like Scene Player can integrate without modifying the core Chat flow.

Summary: 4.7 Suggest follow-up questions from GraphRAG
Description:
As a user,
I want relevant follow-up questions after an answer,
So that I can continue exploring connected people, places, events and cultural themes without knowing what to ask next.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** assistant returns a grounded response `answered` to entity/topic
**When** the system creates follow-up suggestions
**Then** suggest 2 to 4 questions based on evidence, timeline or graph paths 1–2 hops belonging to the same pinned release
**And** each suggestion has a traceable target entity/intent/path basis
**And** don't propose a question just because it sounds interesting but the corpus isn't capable of supporting it.

**Given** graphs have many valid exploration paths
**When** select suggestions
**Then** prioritizes different directions such as relationships, events, comparisons or thematic content
**And** avoid repeating questions that have just been answered or suggestions that are almost the same
**And** does not result in a draft, withdrawn or out-of-scope entity.

**Given** suggestion is inferred by model or template
**When** suggestion is about to return to the UI
**Then** the backend verifies referenced entities/relations/evidence exist in the pinned release
**And** invalid/unverifiable suggestion was rejected
**And** suggestion text is not presented as an answered factual claim.

**Given** the user selects a suggested question
**When** new questions are posted
**Then** it goes through the full resolver, planner, retrieval, evidence and grounding gates like a normal question
**And** do not reuse old answers or bypass evidence gates
**And** conversation keeps the context clearly visible.

**Given** response is `clarify` or `abstained`
**When** UI needs next actions
**Then** only displays clarification/rephrase options or directions for which there is safe evidence
**And** do not use deep-dive suggestions to hide the system's lack of evidence.

**Given** Chat UI render suggestions
**When** the user uses a mouse, keyboard or screen reader
**Then** suggestions are controls with an accessible name and focus state
**And** selecting suggestion clearly indicates that a new question will be submitted
**And** loading/error of suggestions does not remove current answers/citations.

Summary: 4.8 Evaluate assistant quality and performance before release
Description:
As a product owner,
I want reproducible evidence that the assistant retrieves, cites and denies correctly,
So that model, prompt or corpus changes cannot silently reduce answer quality.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** versioned evaluation dataset
**When** run retrieval evaluation
**Then** the dataset covers canonical names, aliases, unaccented text, typing errors, paraphrases, ambiguous queries, and out-of-scope queries
**And** expected entity, intent, operator and evidence are defined independently of the implementation
**And** retrieval recall@1 achieved the target of ≥95% on the published set.

**Given** fixed evidence packages and representative questions
**When** run generation/grounding evaluation
**Then** measures citation faithfulness ≥85%, citation coverage ≥90% and abstention accuracy ≥90%
**And** the three metrics are reported together to avoid skewed optimization
**And** false-premise, conflicting-source, unsupported-number/date cases are checked separately.

**Given** assistant runs in the target demo environment
**When** loads the recorded profile
**Then** chat end-to-end p95 ≤8 seconds or report clearly indicating the gate has not been passed
**And** latency is separated by resolver, retrieval, evidence, inference and post-gate
**And** timeout/error rate is reported at the same quality.

**Given** evaluation completed
**When** report is saved
**Then** report records model/base/adapter or GGUF hash, tokenizer/quantization, prompt version, corpus release, retrieval configuration and dataset version
**And** results can be rerun from the same inputs/configuration
**And** missing metadata makes the report ineligible for release.

**Given** model, prompt, retrieval config or corpus changes
**When** CI/release gate runs regression suite
**Then** the change exceeds the specified degradation threshold to block promotion
**And** answers are not hard-coded merely to make the tests pass
**And** failure cases have a trace/evidence package to investigate without exposing sensitive data.

Summary: Epic 5: Scene-Based, 3D, and Multimedia Heritage Experiences
Description: Users start from Content Landing and progress through a guided story of 1–6 ordered narrative scenes. Each scene combines evidence-backed content with images, panoramas, or 3D viewpoints, hotspots, audio, and transcripts. If a media asset fails, the scene falls back gracefully and the rest of the experience remains functional.

Summary: 5.1 Compile a guided story consisting of 1–6 narrative scenes
Description:
As a knowledge manager,
I want to compose an ordered guided story from evidence-backed narrative scenes,
So that visitors can follow a purposeful experience instead of viewing an unstructured 3D model.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Admin creates a guided story for Content Landing/site
**When** save story draft
